- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 20–40% for spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model underestimates; increase low-range forecasts by 15–30% to avoid missing sharp rebounds.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon outcomes, especially in late-2024 examples — apply 30–50% downward bias to long-term forecasts.
- After a spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 5–7 days — apply “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 15–25% for the next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model fails to anticipate reversal — add 10–20% upward bias to forecast 3–5 days after sentiment turns positive.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and recent history is stable — increase forecast by 5–15% for 3–7 day horizons in such contexts.
